newsitem.title: USA: U.S. cools ties with Belarus over rights problems.
newsitem.headline: U.S. cools ties with Belarus over rights problems.

text.p: The United States said on Friday it had downgraded its relationship with Belarus because of what it called a "serious turn for the worse" in the human rights situation in the former Soviet republic.

Although no changes were announced in diplomatic representation, the State Department said it had recently re-evaluated ties with Belarus and decided on a policy of what it called "selective engagement."
U.S. officials explained that this meant Washington would only be willing to discuss with Belarus matters which were of direct concern to the United States.
"The United States remains seriously concerned about human rights violations in Belarus, particularly in the past several weeks," said State Deaprtment spokesman Nicholas Burns.

Burns said the Belarus government imposed on March 5 what he called severe restrictions on freedom of speech and assembly, and that various political party offices had recently been searched by police.

Burns also cited strong-arm tactics against demonstrators. Reports from the capital Minsk on Friday said police beat people protesting against hardline President Alexander Lukashenko as they cleared an unauthorised rally in the city centre.

The U.S. spokesman called on the Belarus government to show restraint during demonstrations marking Constitution Day on Friday and on Saturday, and to observe international human rights agreements it had signed.
Minsk authorities banned protesters from marching through the capital on Saturday, when opposition forces plan a big rally.

"How Belarus conducts itself, how it treats its own people will have an indelible effect on the U.S. relationship with Belarus," Burns said. "The government of Belarus claims that it tolerates dissent. It's time for a clear demonstration of that pledge."

The United States and other Western powers heaped criticism on Lukashenko, especially for a referendum in November 1996 when he used a landslide win to rewrite the constitution and obtain sweeping powers.
Washington has also been alarmed by attempts by Belarus, which occupies a strategic position between Russia and Poland, to reintegrate with Russia.
